messages:
Sophia: Quick sync — kicking off a short sprint to tighten the competitive battlecard vs cloud AI platforms and infra vendors. Need: 2 benchmark narratives, 6 short soundbites, 3 webinar hooks, and inbound routing tags. Who can own what?
Mike: I can own benchmarks. Plan: cost-per-token, tail latency, and end-to-end sec/ops story vs CloudX and APIY. Need expected seq-length buckets and common batch sizes.
Ana: I'll take messaging + soundbites. Focus should be on production economics + graceful degradation. Short, snappy lines for SDRs.
James: Webinar hook idea: "How to cut LLM inference cost without blowing up latency" — 20m demo (routing + fallback), 20m talk, 20m live Q&A. Works for PLG-to-enterprise.
Marco: For inbound routing tags, recommend: `enterprise-sla`, `latency-sensitive`, `regulated-data`, `proof-of-scale`. SDRs can map tags -> playbook.
Sophia: Mike, please sync w/ Eli from eng-ml for microbench numbers and a short notes doc. Ana, can you draft 4 quick rebut lines vs the "we already run it on cloud" objection?
Eli: Shared prelim bench plan in #eng-ml. We’ll provide numbers for 256/1024/2048 seq, batch sizes 1/8/32, and quantized variants by EOD. Can also include KV-cache savings for chat patterns.
Mike: Thanks @Eli — that'll let us make a clean claim set: typical p50/p95 token latency, tail latency impact of batching, and cost per 1M tokens.
Ana: Drafted two messaging tones and pasted below: 
- Pragmatic: "Predictable unit economics for inference — reduce surprise spend with routing, caching, and quantization."
- Assertive: "Don't buy GPUs, buy predictable inference — same output quality at 1/3rd the operational cost."
Ana: Also 6 SDR-ready soundbites: 
`1` "Production LLMs: predictable, observable, and affordable."
`2` "Fallbacks keep your app live when models or regions falter."
`3` "Batching & cache = instant wins for cost/latency."
`4` "Pin a model version, run canaries, avoid regressions."
`5` "Enterprise SLAs, not surprise bills."
`6` "We unify hosted, dedicated, and private with one API."
James: Love the webinar structure. For demo, show live routing: high-accuracy model for long queries, low-cost variant for short ones, automatic fallback. Keep slide deck under 12 slides + demo.
Marco: Routing tags snippet for SDRs (copyable):
```
if lead.tags contains ("enterprise-sla" or "regulated-data") then route -> AE_enterprise;
else if lead.tags contains "latency-sensitive" then route -> Solutions_latency;
else route -> PLG_inbound
```
Sophia: Nice — can we add a default follow-up template for SDRs to use? Short, includes claim + CTA.
Ana: Draft follow-up: "Hey {{name}}, noticed you're latency-sensitive — we cut inference cost while keeping p95 under your SLO. Quick 15m to show a routing + fallback config?"
marketing-bot: Reminder: update the battlecard doc at https://docs.redwood.ai/battlecards/obsidian by EOD Friday. :bell:
Sophia: OK — owners: Mike (benchmarks & numbers), Ana (soundbites + rebut lines + SDR templates), James (webinar logistics + deck), Marco (inbound routing rules). Eli to supply bench artifacts. I'll collate for the Friday review. :thumbsup:
Mike: I'll post preliminary numbers in the doc and ping Product for claim sign-off.
Eli: Sharing a CSV + a small gif of the demo run later today.
Sophia: Thanks team — we'll review Friday 09:30. If anyone needs to swap ownership shout here.
